text:
alex: Customer (acme-health) opened an escalation — private API endpoint returning intermittent 503s and auth failures since ~02:00 UTC. They say traffic went over ExpressRoute->VPC peering and flipped to IPsec fallback during the window. Error shown in app logs: "upstream response: 503 Service Unavailable; failed to fetch from 10.2.5.8"

lee: Can you paste a minimal repro and whether this is consistently reproducible from their side? Also which routing mode (HC or advertising customer prefixes)?

alex: Repro steps from customer: 1) curl -v https://private-api.acme.internal/health -> sometimes 200, often 503. 2) SDK calls fail with KMS auth: "tls: handshake error: remote error: tls: bad certificate". They provided a tcpdump and an ipsec status excerpt. Attaching snippets inline:

--- tcpdump snippet ---
12:03:14.123 IP 10.0.5.12.443 > 10.2.5.8.53942: Flags [P.], seq..., ack...
12:03:14.324 IP 10.2.5.8.53942 > 10.0.5.12.443: Flags [R], seq 0, ack 0

--- strongSwan status ---
Security Associations (1 up, 0 connecting):
	peer 203.0.113.1[CN=acme-gw] established IKE SA
	established CHILD_SA with ESP; installed

(sometimes we see IKE AUTH failures in logs: "AUTH_FAILED")

sre_oncall: I'm seeing BGP flaps in our peering logs around 02:01:12 UTC, neighbor 169.254.100.1 went DOWN then came back. That matches the customer's flap window. Can you paste BGP neighbor outputs from acme side?

maria-cust: From our side:
- BGP neighbor 169.254.100.1: state ESTABLISHED now, but we saw multiple NOTIFICATION messages.
- DNS: calls to kms.internal.acme resolve intermittently. dig @10.0.0.53 kms.internal.acme ANY -> sometimes NXDOMAIN then answers.
- TLS traces: openssl s_client -connect kms.internal.acme:443 shows timeout when DNS NXDOMAIN occurs.

netops-jordan: Two hypotheses: 1) BGP flap caused asymmetric routing -> some responses egress via alternate path where return reachability fails and resets TCP sessions. 2) Peering change impacted route targets for private DNS or split-horizon records, causing intermittent NXDOMAINs which break TLS (SNI lookup for mTLS cert pinning). Also OCSP/CRL reachability could be blocked by egress allowlists.

alex: I checked our side: service instances report upstream 10.2.5.8 healthy locally. Console trace shows TLS handshake failure to KMS host with error "certificate verify failed: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority" in ~30% of traces. Could be the KMS endpoint seen as different due to DNS bounce.

lee: Can we get a tcpdump from one of our private workers (10.2.5.8) showing SYN/SYN-ACK/RST sequences and look for asymmetric src/dst? Also capture IPsec logs (charon) and BGP syslog for the same window.

alex: Uploaded captures from worker-3 -> attached gist link: https://internal-gists/acme/1765559876-capture (redacted). Key lines: repeated TCP RSTs from peer 203.0.113.1 right after SYN-ACK. ipsec charon shows occasional AUTH_FAILED with IKEv2 AUTH payload mismatch.

netops-jordan: I correl'd with our cloud-provider ExpressRoute change request 99321 (deploy-bot posted it). Provider did a path maintenance at 02:00 and briefly suppressed a set of routes, causing BGP NOTIFICATION/withdrawals for a couple minutes. When routes returned, traffic used the backup IPsec path that had stale certificate/tunnel configuration on the remote side -> IKE AUTH failing intermittently.

deploy-bot: deploy event: expressroute-maintenance/99321 completed at 2025-05-14T02:00:43Z by ops-scheduler.

maria-cust: We also discovered our DNS forwarding was split across two resolvers; one resolver was routing over the old, partially-broken path and returned stale NXDOMAIN for private zones. That explains intermittent DNS and TLS failures.

sre_oncall: Immediate mitigations proposed: 1) request provider to confirm full route propagation and BGP neighbor stability (open ticket and attach BGP dumps). 2) Ask customer to fail back to primary ExpressRoute circuit or re-establish IPsec child SA with refreshed certs/PSK. 3) Temporarily add explicit egress allowlist entries for OCSP + KMS IPs to avoid external routing via backup path. 4) Add health-check gating so backend clients retry DNS if NXDOMAIN then fallback to alternate resolver.

alex: Action items assigned:
- netops-jordan -> open support ticket with provider, include our BGP/RIB/tcpdump (ETA 30m).
- maria-cust -> rotate IPsec certs/confirm IKE AUTH config on their gateway (they did a cert reissue in thread).
- lee -> add temporary egress allowlist for KMS and OCSP endpoints in customer's VPC NAT rules and confirm not blocked by firewall.

netops-jordan: Ticket opened with provider #MSFT-IR-77412, forwarded dumps. Provider acknowledges transient route withdrawal, working on ensuring all route-propagation complete.

maria-cust: Rotated certs and forced child SA rekey at 03:10 UTC. After that, we saw TLS handshakes succeed and SDK auth errors drop to ~0.5% from ~35%. DNS still had occasional NXDOMAIN for ~5 minutes until resolver sticky cache flushed.

alex: Can you confirm service health now? Any lingering 5xx?

maria-cust: After 03:20 UTC customer confirms steady 200 responses and KMS auth ok. They asked for a short postmortem and prevention checklist.

sre_oncall: Marking incident resolved. Follow-ups: - PM to request provider scheduled maintenance windows include route dampening exemptions for private peering - engineering to add a DNS fallback resolver config for Private mode - ops to document IPsec cert rotation SOP to avoid AUTH_FAILED during peering failovers.

lee: Thanks everyone. I'll kick off a short postmortem draft and tag @netops-jordan and @maria-cust for details. :thumbsup:

alex: Closing thread — will upload captures + timeline to ops-incident repo.
